option.label: Lower blade margins with papilla-based hairs
option.detail: Gould locates sparse papilla-based marginal hairs on the lower blade margins. These are not upper-glume midnerve hairs or a ligule fringe.

option.label: Long hairs at the sheath throat
option.detail: Inspect the sheath opening, separately from the inner ligule. Gould describes pilose throat, with sheath body hairless or lowermost sheaths thinly hairy.

option.label: Branch rachis projects as a bare point
option.detail: Trace the branch AXIS beyond its final spikelet. Gould reports 5–8 mm or more; this is not a lemma awn or an axis-like terminal rudimentary spikelet.

option.label: FIRST glume minutely stiff-hairy
option.detail: First outer glume 1.5–3 mm, minutely hispid. Do not transfer second-glume long midnerve hairs to this smaller glume.

option.label: SECOND glume with long papilla-based midnerve hairs
option.detail: Second outer glume 3–5 mm, bearing 1–2 mm papilla-based hairs on midnerve. Not hairs on a sessile FIRST glume or on a blade.

option.label: SECOND glume minutely awned at tip
option.detail: Locate the upper OUTER glume. A minute awn at its apex is not evidence that the fertile lemma has the same awn.

option.label: FERTILE lemma finely hairy on back
option.detail: Gould describes the perfect-floret lemma, 5–6 mm long, as more or less puberulent on the back. This is different from glume midnerve hairs.

option.label: LOWER rudimentary floret: three rough awns
option.detail: Within one spikelet find the lower of TWO rudimentary florets, above the perfect floret. Its three hispid awns are about 4 mm. Do not assign these three awns to the fertile lemma.

option.label: UPPER rudimentary floret: minute scale
option.detail: Gould describes the upper rudimentary floret as a tiny scale, separate from the three-awned lower rudiment and perfect floret.

option.label: Rachilla below LOWER rudiment hairless
option.detail: Inspect only the rachilla segment below the lower rudimentary floret. Gould states it is not hairy; keep broader FNA variation/source scope visible rather than generalizing all rachilla segments.

evidence.note: Blades 1–2 mm broad. Thread is usual; 2 mm lies on the shared approximate narrow boundary.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Identify each floret before counting awns
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould has one perfect floret and two rudimentary florets: the lower rudiment has THREE hispid awns about 4 mm, the upper is a minute scale. The perfect lemma is separately 5–6 mm and finely hairy on its back.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not transfer the rudimentary floret’s three awns to the fertile lemma, or silently replace the existing FNA fertile-awn evidence.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould p.353; broader FNA floret/awn variation preserved separately.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Bouteloua hirsuta, printed p.353

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Follow the branch axis beyond the final spikelet
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould reports a pointed branch rachis extending 5–8 mm or more beyond the last spikelet. Diggs independently distinguishes a continuous projecting axis in hairy grama from tall grama’s axis-like rudimentary terminal spikelet.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: The left-page figure is BLUE grama, not hairy grama. Tall grama below is a separate taxon; its terminal structure must not be imported.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould p.353 / Diggs p.1249 named treatments; no diagram/photo relabeling.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Bouteloua hirsuta, printed p.353

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate glume midnerve, culm node and rachilla hairs
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: First glume minutely stiff-hairy; second has long papilla-based midnerve hairs and a minute apical awn. Culm nodes hairless. Gould says rachilla below the lower rudiment is not hairy; the older broader FNA rachilla variation remains flagged.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: These are different organs from KR’s sessile first-glume back, pedicel margins and culm-node beard. A lack of description does not establish a missing KR trait.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Organ and segment scope preserved; no new hard exclusion from source conflict.

secondary_reference_review.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, exact Bouteloua hirsuta and B.pectinata comparisons
secondary_reference_review.access: Directly read owner-connected reference PDF; following POACEAE/BOUTELOUA1249 footer verified.
secondary_reference_review.corroborates: Hairy: 1–4 straight/curved branches 2.3–4 cm including tip; continuous axis extends beyond spikelets. Tall: axis not extended, axis-like terminal rudimentary spikelet usually hairy at base, bifid at apex; recognized separately with historical hirsuta subspecies names.
secondary_reference_review.scope: Do not treat broad FNA hirsuta concepts as automatically identical to Gould/Diggs separate-species treatments.
